However, the High Court further held that since the appellants had not received compensation determined under the 1894 Act, the respondents were required to pay the same along with the other benefits flowing from the provisions of the Act of 1894, within a time frame.
The operative part of the High Courts order reads as follows:

Though, the petitioners are not entitled  to compensation under the Act of 2013, since, the  petitioners have not received the compensation  determined under the Act of 1894 till date, it would  be necessary to direct the respondents to pay the  same to the petitioners along with the other benefits  flowing from the provisions of the Act of 1894,

4. It appears that after the above directions were issued by the High Court, the compensation amount was deposited vide Cheque No.647102 dated 05.12.2014, before the High Court.
Since the said amount did not include interest in terms of Section 34 of the 1894 Act, the appellants raised such a claim, which has been declined by the High Court.
3 5. It is an admitted fact that the compensation was awarded to the appellants on 09.07.2009 but actual payment was made on 05.12.2014.
The compensation amount during this period was retained by the respondents.
The award of interest as per Section 34 of the 1894 Act, is one of the statutory benefits which an ex-propriated land owner is entitled to.

Since the High Court vide the impugned judgment dated 25.09.2019, had held the appellants entitled to the statutory benefits under the 1894 Act, it is imperative on the respondents to pay interest to the appellants for the period from 23.07.2009 to 05.12.2014, in accordance with Section 34 of the 1894 Act.

6. For the reasons aforestated, the appeal is allowed, the impugned order dated 25.09.2019, passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur is set aside and the appellants are held entitled to interest, as directed above.
